Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Light direction: backlit — the main light comes from behind her, a bright rim along her hair and shoulders.
Outfit: a vampire countess costume — a high-collared velvet cape over a fitted gown with a cinched waist — in warm sand beige; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance; right now — the slit or wrap of her skirt has fallen open along one thigh with her movement, baring that leg up to the hip line; the fabric stays in place, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

SUPPORT: she sits on the edge, her weight on her hips.
COMPOSITION: a three-quarter shot from her head to just above the knees; body facing the camera; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
BOTH HANDS: both hands brace on the edge on either side of her hips.
LEGS: knees together, feet slightly apart.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: level brow, calm unhurried eyes, mouth closed and composed.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — thallium: a soft grey metal that cuts with a knife, dulls quickly in air and is kept under oil; found in 1861 by a London chemist who saw a single vivid spring-green line in the spectrum of sulfuric-acid works residue and named it from the Greek for a green shoot, and while weighing it in a vacuum he came upon the little sun-spun light mill; its salts dissolve in water with no taste or smell, the poisoner's poison, slipping into the body by passing as potassium and making hair fall out, with Prussian blue as its antidote; that same disguise lets a trace of it map where blood reaches the heart muscle, and mixed with mercury it reads temperatures far below freezing — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: petite and short in stature yet voluptuous — a very full, heavy bust, a narrow waist and generously rounded hips on a small, compact frame, with realistic thighs and legs — keep this exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
